C: B1 [ C ] an amount of money

S: › [ S ] the whole number or amount when two or more numbers or amounts have been added together
總的來說，總而言之，總之
› all of something, especially when this is not very much

C: › [ C ] a calculation, especially a simple one, using such processes as adding, taking away, multiplying, or dividing
（尤指運用加減乘除的簡單）計算，算術

example: Huge sums of money are spent on national defence.
巨額的錢財都投入到國防上。
He sold the house for a tidy (= large) sum.
他把房子賣了一大筆錢。
The meeting was, in sum, a disaster.
總而言之，這次會議糟糕透了。
And that's the sum of my knowledge on the subject!
恐怕我對這個學科的了解總共就那麼一點點！
I remember how much I hated doing sums when I was at school.
我記得我上學的時候非常討厭算術。

NONE: B2 to describe or express the important facts or characteristics about something or someone
總結，概述，概括
› An action or object that sums something or someone up represents the most typical qualities of that person or thing.
代表，體現
› to quickly form an opinion about someone or something
對…迅速作出判斷

example: The best way of summing up the situation in our office is to say that it is "absolute chaos".
一言以蔽之，我們辦公室的情況「完全是一團糟」。
I'd just like to sum up by saying that it's been a tremendous pleasure to work with you.
總之，跟您合作真是一大樂事。
He's a small man with a big ego - that about sums him up.
他是個自高自大的小個子男人——這樣都差不多概括他了。
For me, her paintings sum up the restless spirit of America.
在我看來，她的畫集中表現了自強不息的美國精神。
She summed up the situation quickly and took charge.
她很快對形勢作出判斷並開始主持工作。

NONE: › The sum total of something is the whole of it, or everything
全部；總量；總和

example: It's the sum total of what you eat over a long period that matters and not what you consume in a day.
重要的是你長期所吃的食物總和，而不是你某一天所吃的東西。

NONE: › When a judge sums up towards the end of a trial, he or she makes a speech to the jury telling them again of the main matters they should consider in the case.
（審理結束前法官向陪審團）作案件總結，作結案陳詞
› at the highest level of the special levels of achievement in a person's studies at a US college or university. The expression comes from Latin, meaning "with the highest praise"
（源自拉丁語，美國大學的）最優等的

example: Danielle graduated summa cum laude.
丹妮耶拉以最優等的成績畢業。
a summa cum laude graduate
一名獲得最優等的畢業生。
See also
cum laude

NONE: C1 to express the most important facts or ideas about something or someone in a short and clear form
總結，概述，概括

example: I'll just summarize the main points of the argument in a few words.
我會用幾句話把爭論的要點概括一下。
To summarize, we believe the company cannot continue in its present form.
總而言之，我們認為公司不能再以目前的方式繼續經營下去。

NONE: B2 a short, clear description that gives the main facts or ideas about something
總結，概要，摘要
› done suddenly, without discussion or legal arrangements
（未經討論或法律程式）立即的，速決的，草率的

example: At the end of the news, they often give you a summary of the main stories.
在新聞結束的時候，他們常常會總結一下主要的新聞內容。
In summary, they decided against the proposal.
總而言之，他們決定反對這項提議。

NONE: › something
某事；某物

example: There's summat wrong with this machine.
這臺機器出了點問題。

NONE: › formal a short, clear description that gives the main facts or ideas about something
總結
› formal something that represents a complete account or impression of what someone or something is like
對…的概括
› US specialized law a speech made by a judge or lawyer to the jury towards the end of a trial, telling them again about the main matters they should consider in the case
（審判結束前，法官或律師的）法庭辯論總結，最後陳詞

example: He offered his own concise summation of the problem.
他用自己的方式對問題作了精要的總結。
The scene where the two characters dance is the perfect summation of the love and desire between them.
兩人雙雙起舞的場面完美地概括了他們之間的愛與渴望。
the prosecutor's final summation
控方的最後陳詞

NONE: A1 the season of the year between spring and autumn when the weather is warmest, lasting from June to September north of the equator and from December to March south of the equator
夏天，夏季
› to spend the summer in a particular place
（在某個地方）度過夏天

example: We have breakfast on the balcony in (the) summer.
夏天，我們在陽臺上吃早飯。
Last summer they went to Australia, and two summers ago they went to Brazil.
去年夏天他們去了澳大利亞，前年夏天他們去了巴西。
That year it was a hot, dry summer.
去年夏天又熱又乾燥。
a summer/summer's day
一個夏日

NONE: › in the US, a place where children can go, usually to stay, and do activities
（美國）夏令營

example: Her children were away at summer camp.
她的孩子都去了夏令營。

NONE: › a cold, sweet dish consisting of several soft, red and purple fruits, such as raspberries and blackberries, surrounded by bread
（將山莓、藍莓等水果夾在麵包中製成的）夏令布丁
› an educational course that happens during the summer holidays
暑期班，暑假課程
› US one or more classes taken during the summer that replace classes that were missed or failed, or make it possible for students to move more quickly towards a degree or graduation
（為補足因缺課、不及格失去的學分或為加快學生學習進度以盡早拿到學位或畢業而開辦的）暑期學校，暑期補習班

example: They organize an annual summer school for young musicians.
他們為青年樂手組織一年一度的暑期課程。
The students had improved enough after summer school to be promoted to 4th grade.
這些學生在暑期補習班提高了很多，有資格升入四年級了。

NONE: › a small building in a garden used for sitting in during the summer
（花園中的）涼亭，涼棚
› US a house at the beach or in the mountains that you live in for part or all of the summer
（海濱或山中的）避暑別墅
› the season of summer
夏天，夏季

example: You should see the flower garden in (the) summertime - it's beautiful.
你應該在夏天的時候來看看這個花園——非常漂亮。

NONE: › typical of or suitable for summer
夏天的；適合夏季的

example: Clare walked by looking very summery in a pale blue sundress.
克萊爾穿著淺藍色的太陽裙，渾身散發著夏日氣息。

NONE: › a speech made by a judge or lawyer to the jury towards the end of a trial, telling them again about the main matters they should consider in the case
（審判結束前，法官或律師的）法庭辯論總結，最後陳詞

example: The judge referred to this point several times in his summing-up.
法官在最後陳詞中幾次提到了這一點。

C: C2 an important formal meeting between leaders of governments from two or more countries
高峰會，領袖會議，最高級會議
C1 the highest point of a mountain
› the highest, most successful, or most important point in something

example: a summit meeting
高峰會議
World leaders will meet next week for their annual economic summit.
世界各國領袖將在下週齊聚一堂，參加一年一度的經濟高峰會。
On this day in 1784, Dr Michel Paccard and Jacques Balmat reached the summit of Mont Blanc.
1784年的今天，麥克‧帕卡德醫生和雅克‧巴爾馬特登上了勃朗峰的頂峰。
I certainly haven't reached the summit of my career.
當然，我還沒有達到事業的巔峰。

T: C2 to order someone to come to or be present at a particular place, or to officially arrange a meeting of people
命令…到（某地）；傳喚；召喚；召集
C2 to increase your courage or strength, especially with an effort
（尤指努力地）鼓起（勇氣），積聚（力氣）

example: General Rattigan summoned reinforcements to help resist the attack.
拉蒂根將軍命令增援部隊協助抵擋進攻。
On 20 July, the town council was summoned to hear an emergency report on its finances.
7月20日，鎮政務委員會被召集起來聽取有關其財務問題的緊急報告。
We were summoned to the headmaster's office.
我們被叫去了校長辦公室。
It took me six months to summon (up) the courage to ask him out for a drink.
我花了六個月時間才鼓起勇氣約他出去喝一杯。

NONE: › law an official demand to appear in a law court
（法庭的）傳喚，傳訊，傳票
› formal an order to come and see someone
命令；召喚

example: He was given/served with a summons to appear in court.
他被傳喚出庭。
Mr Clarke's insurance company had issued a summons for unpaid mortgage repayments.
克拉克先生的保險公司已就未償還的按揭貸款提起訴訟。
They sat there as if they were waiting for some sort of summons.
他們坐在那裡，仿佛是在等待召喚。

NONE: › a style of wrestling (= a fighting sport) originally from Japan, in which each man tries to defeat the other either by pushing him outside of a special ring or by forcing him to touch the ground with a part of his body other than the bottom part of the foot
相撲（運動）
› a hole or container, especially in the lower part of an engine, into which a liquid that is not needed can flow
污水坑，集液池；（尤指引擎下部的）機油箱
› luxurious and showing that you are rich
奢侈的，豪華的，奢華的

example: The celebrity guests turned up dressed in sumptuous evening gowns.
名流們身著奢華的晚禮服盛裝出席。
